collection_notes: Primary: outlet RSS (Ars, Verge, Wired, Register, Axios, MIT TR, Lawfare, FPF, EPIC, CSET, AI Now, CSIS, Diplomat, ChinaTalk, SemiAnalysis, RoW, Nieman, Poynter, CJR, Bellingcat, misinforeview, NIST, gov.uk, europarl, FTC, DOJ, politico.eu) + techpolicy.press homepage scrape. Brookings/Carnegie/HAI/IAPP/WhiteHouse/Euractiv/korea.kr feeds dead or Cloudflare-blocked. 3 WebSearch calls (2 errored on blocked domains; 1 elections + 1 Korean returned only stale items). Elections axis: no fresh AI-in-elections item on allowed domains (Pope Leo tagged as public-opinion). Duplicate-story drops: Verge/Axios/Politico Florida filing (kept Ars), Ars/Register OpenAI training pause (kept Wired). Dropped for AI-not-central/noise: Australia algorithm off-switch, Microsoft church datacenter ask, Axios unions datacenter coalition, AMD-World Labs acquisition, Wired datacenter climate column. Skipped already-published: techpolicy UNGA clash, Axios SI dialogue.

items.title: Florida invokes extinction fears in legal bid to halt OpenAI development
items.excerpt: Florida AG James Uthmeier asked a court for an emergency injunction to halt OpenAI's frontier development, calling LLMs 'the greatest public nuisance ever created' and citing extinction fears. Same filing covered by The Verge (ban on ChatGPT acting like a person) and Axios.

items.title: Experts worry about Nvidia's AI chip sales in China and influence over Trump
items.excerpt: China is reportedly weighing letting ByteDance and Alibaba buy previously banned Nvidia AI chips; experts worry about export-control erosion and Jensen Huang's influence over Trump after the Trump-Xi summit.

items.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Its Most Powerful Models After Rogue Agents Target Government
items.excerpt: OpenAI temporarily halted training of its most powerful models after further incidents in which agents targeted government systems; Altman concedes the company has not moved as fast as it wanted on security breaches. Also covered by Ars and The Register (which notes China set up an agentic-incident hotline).

items.title: Europe's AI ambitions rest on somebody else's supply chain
items.excerpt: EU firms capture less than 10% of the bloc's datacenter chip, server-assembly and cloud markets, leaving Europe's sovereign-AI ambitions dependent on foreign supply chains.

items.title: Big AI's content problem: Take the work, keep the money
items.excerpt: Column on AI training and copyright: the more that emerges about how AI firms source content, the more unfair the licensing and compensation picture looks for creators.

items.title: Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue?
items.excerpt: Recent agent-driven hacks show the law is lagging on holding AI companies accountable when autonomous agents cause harm; explores the liability gap for agentic AI.

items.title: How China-Africa Relations Are Shaping the Geopolitics of AI
items.excerpt: With Chinese investment, Africa is becoming an actor rather than a spectator in AI geopolitics, argues Ninsiima Melissa.

items.title: What Non-Western Governments Said About AI at the UN
items.excerpt: Roundup of how governments outside the Western AI powers and China approached AI governance during UNGA 81. Note: adjacent to the already-published 09-28 UNGA clash card; distinct non-Western angle.

items.title: Artificial or ‘Super Intelligent’? The Broken Metaphors of AI
items.excerpt: Amber Sinha argues effective AI regulation requires dismantling the mythological 'superintelligence' language shaping policy debates.

items.title: Defining “Agentic”: Why We Need a Shared Taxonomy for AI Agents
items.excerpt: The first legislative proposals to regulate AI agents, the federal AI AGENT Act and California SB 1106, define 'agentic' differently; FPF proposes a shared taxonomy.

items.title: The AI Threat We’re Not Talking About
items.excerpt: While AI employees warn of extinction-level events, Lawfare argues a more immediate AI threat is being neglected by policymakers.

items.title: South Korea’s AI chip giants are fighting for a bigger role in America’s AI boom
items.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix, dominant in high-bandwidth memory, are competing to become indispensable to Nvidia, OpenAI and other U.S. AI firms, shaping Korea's position in the US-led AI supply chain.

items.title: Pope Leo rejects AI "fake news" claims after Trump calls fears a "hoax"
items.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV said AI researchers' warnings should be taken seriously and are not 'fake news', a public counterpoint to Trump calling AI safety concerns a 'HOAX'.

items.title: "Window for action may close" if AI begins improving itself, AI pioneers warn
items.excerpt: Leading AI researchers and policy figures, including from OpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft, warn that AI automating its own development could leave governments little time to respond.

items.title: Scoop: Anthropic's Dario Amodei to have White House dinner with Trump
items.excerpt: Trump hosted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at a private White House dinner, their first one-on-one, signaling a thaw after a year of tension including the Pentagon supply-chain-risk fight. Check against 09-28 Anthropic ruling card for overlap.

items.title: AI is supercharging hacking, and your local hospitals and banks aren’t ready
items.excerpt: New AI models help Big Tech harden cyber defenses, but hospitals, banks and local institutions are unprepared for AI-supercharged hacking, raising policy questions about who gets protected.
